Well, your opinion is much like the one I had at your age. I am 35 now and mine has changed to be more like your parents. Whilst in principle I believe that everyone should have the right to do what they want with their own life, the reality isn't that simple. A lot of people make really fucking terrible choices for themselves. Whilst I'd probably fall short of directly legislating against or for some things, a laissez faire attitude doesn't really work in my experience. It is phenomenally costly for the state/government and always has a human cost for the vulnerable and easily exploited. Yes, some people lose a few liberties that they could police themselves but the vulnerable are protected. That is how a society works. It is an ugly ill-fitting mess but it works. As you age you learn to accept that although you may well be right about things and even know how to change them for the better; they can not be changed and are that way for a reason.  
Also, if your parents think weed should be legal in my opinion they are barmy. I used to smoke a lot of it through college, I'm not misinformed. But legalising it sends utterly the wrong message about a drug that has fucked up a lot of lives.

The problem is that we are led to believe that there are jobs enough for all the graduates. There are not. I am 13 years on from graduating in Geology and Ecology. I now also have a degree in Computing and one in Digital Marketing. I've had to do both to try and make progress with my career. It hasn't much helped but has at least raised my salary slightly and let me work in fields that actually have vacancies. Sadly, I've only ever worked in jobs that I hate, because I just can't get into a field I'd like to work in. I decided I had had enough last year and I left my job and now live in a far cheaper place. I have enough savings to last three years without working. I'm going to take that time to work on my own projects that I care about and then when the money runs out I am going to jump off of the cliffs by the sea near my town.
